question.value: Characterize the ISM conditions, kinematics, morphology and star formation of seven extremely luminous Hot DOGs.

evidence.quote: In this work we study a sample of seven of the most luminous Hot DOGs, at redshifts *z* $\sim$ 3.0–4.6, observed with ALMA in the \[C ii\]$_{158}$  line.
In this section we discuss how the presence of an extremely luminous (EL) AGN
ALMA targeted the \[C ii\]  emission line for the sample of seven Hot DOGs under programs 2013.1.00576.S (W0116–0505, W0134–2922, W0220+0137 and W2246–0526)
Owing to their redshifts, W2246–0526 was observed in band 7 and the remaining galaxies in band 8.

All four SPWs were usable for all sources and no additional flagging was needed.

referee_caveats_inferred: Resolve internal numerical inconsistencies before constructing strict answer keys: several velocity offsets differ between tables and prose.
The summary extended-[C ii] fraction range does not include the approximately 95–96% value reported for W0831+0140 elsewhere.
W2246–0526 dynamical mass depends strongly on the support assumption despite substantial model residuals.
Extended emission need not be powered exclusively by star formation; treating it as AGN-free can bias SFR estimates.
Extended fractions depend on resolution, so comparisons require matched beams.
Stellar masses use a Chabrier IMF while the quoted SFR conversion uses a Kroupa IMF; the text gives no harmonization procedure.
Four robust line detections and heterogeneous comparison samples limit population-level interpretation of the KS result.
The main-sequence discussion lists overlapping source counts; individual classifications should be checked against the plotted estimates.
